findings.title: sanitizeTrackingParams silently drops utm_* params whose key contains malformed percent-encoding: the occurrence-scan key decoder (native decodeURIComponent with raw fallback) diverges from queryString.parse's key decoder (decode-uri-component, lenient)
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC §5.1 (D4): utmData holds "every other param whose name starts with utm_"; contract "order comes from the raw string, values from the parse". No rule permits dropping a utm_* param that queryString.parse captured. Not listed in REVIEW-ANGLES.md as an approved deviation.
findings.evidence: app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js key scan (~lines 41-50) decodes scanned keys with decodeURIComponent (raw-key fallback on throw); query-string v6.1.0 parse() decodes keys with decode-uri-component 0.2.0 (best-effort, U+FFFD replacement). On mixed valid/malformed percent sequences the scan key never matches any parse key, the membership filter parsedParams[key] !== undefined fails, and the param is dropped from utmData entirely (not captured, not counted toward the 10-key cap). Empirically reproduced by two independent agents against the installed libraries: '?utm_x%C2=1&utm_medium=m' → utmData {utm_medium} only; also 'utm_%C3%A9%', 'utm_a%FE%FF', 'utm_%E2%98%83%E2', 'utm_100%25%E2'. Top-level utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref literal-name reads unaffected; params are dropped, never mis-valued.
findings.recommendation: Make the scan's key decoding identical to queryString.parse's for all inputs — use the same decode-uri-component decoder (already in node_modules as query-string 6.1.0's direct dependency) or otherwise guarantee scan-key/parse-key identity. Add a Jest regression case with a mixed-validity encoded utm_* key pinning that it lands in utmData.

findings.title: Jest coverage gap (§9.6): no test asserts the per-value sanitization rules (255-char truncation, first-of-repeated-array) for values INSIDE utmData
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC §9.6 requires Jest coverage of the §5.1 sanitization contract; §5.1 (D4) applies the rules per value ("each value sanitized"), including utmData values. Ghost-test discipline (pipeline rule 26): every contract rule must be falsified by an implementation that omits it.
findings.evidence: app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.test.js: truncation and repeated-param tests exercise only top-level utm_source. An implementation assigning utmData[key] = parsedParams[key] without sanitizeTrackingValue would pass all 8 tests. The current implementation is correct; the rule is unpinned.
